Plot function-to-taxon contributions as grouped boxplots

fun2tax_box.Rd

This function takes a stratified PICRUSt2 output table, a phyloseq object, and a list of pathway-level results, and produces ggplot2 boxplots of function contributions summarized by taxonomic level and experimental group.

Usage

fun2tax_box(
  stratified_path,
  pathway_sdaa_result,
  physeq,
  group,
  taxon_level = NULL,
  pathway = c("KO", "EC", "MetaCyc"),
  value_col = NULL,
  wrap_width = 36,
  group_functions = TRUE
)

Arguments

stratified_path

Character string. Path to a stratified PICRUSt2 output file (typically `*_stratified.tsv`), containing columns for function, taxon, sample, and contribution values.

pathway_sdaa_result

A named list of results from an SDAA (statistical differential abundance analysis) step, keyed by function IDs. Only names are used here.

physeq

A phyloseq object containing sample metadata and taxonomy table. Sample IDs must match those in stratified_path.

group

Character scalar. Column name in sample metadata to use for grouping (e.g. treatment).

taxon_level

Taxonomy rank inferred from the result metadata; defaults to Genus for legacy lists without metadata. Conflicting explicit ranks are rejected.

pathway

Character scalar. Functional annotation scheme used: one of "KO", "EC", or "MetaCyc". Defaults to "KO".

value_col

Character scalar. Name of the numeric contribution column in the stratified table. Defaults to the column recorded in the SDAA result or the PICRUSt2 abundance column when available.

wrap_width

Integer. Width (in characters) for line-wrapping taxon labels on the x-axis. Defaults to 36.

group_functions

Logical. Whether to group function IDs into higher-level reference categories (via reference maps included in the package). Defaults to TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example with KO pathway
plots <- fun2tax_box(
  stratified_path = "ko_metagenome_out_stratified.tsv",
  pathway_sdaa_result = sdaa_result,
  physeq = physeq_obj,
  group = "Treatment",
  taxon_level = NULL,
  pathway = "KO"
)
# Display first plot
print(plots[[1]])
} # }
